metadata.description: A network edge gateway — routing / NAT / firewalling between network segments and to external networks. Grounded in the Kubernetes Gateway API 'Gateway' concept (a network entry/exit point); note UDLM's Network.Gateway is L3/edge (router/NAT/firewall), broader than the Gateway API's L4/L7 service focus. Vendor specifics (a firewall distribution or a vendor firewall appliance) are the provider/extension.

segments.description: Network segments the gateway bridges/routes between.

role.description: Segment role, e.g. wan | lan | dmz | mgmt.

vlan_ref.description: Reference to Network.VLAN — the VLAN this gateway segment serves. Common-elements Reference shape (handle string or {uuid, handle} object); resolvable and policy-walkable, never an opaque string.

external_address.description: Public/WAN address the gateway presents (NAT egress / ingress) once Realized.

relationships.description: Segments the gateway routes may have DHCP scopes served elsewhere.

relationships.name: segment_vlan
relationships.description: segment_vlan — each segment rides a Network.VLAN, referenced (vlan_ref), not an inline 802.1Q id (R5; foundational-resources selected-not-invented).

context.purpose: Models the network edge — routing, NAT, and firewalling between segments and to the outside — as a node the graph can reason about.
context.plain_description: The router/firewall at the edge of a network: which functions it provides (routing, NAT, firewall, VPN) and which segments it connects, each segment referencing the VLAN it rides. The vendor box or software (a firewall distribution, a vendor firewall appliance) is a provider. Detailed routing tables and firewall rulesets are not modeled — the portable surface is functions and segments; once realized it publishes the external address it presents.
use_when: You need what connects this network to the outside as an explicit node with its segments.
You need segment boundaries (LAN, DMZ, mgmt) and their VLANs recorded at the edge that routes between them.
not_for: An L2 switch — Network.Switch; the gateway is the L3 edge.
Service-level L4/L7 traffic entry (the Kubernetes Gateway API sense) — that is the adopted naming ancestor, but this type is the broader network edge; application ingress belongs to the platform.
Handing out addresses on its segments — Network.DHCPScope / Network.AddressService.
works_with: Network.VLAN — each gateway segment rides a referenced VLAN.
Network.DHCPScope — scopes serving the segments the gateway routes.
Network.Switch — the fabric behind the edge.
